subject: PrivFleet network boundary recon & runway projections
messages:

Subject: PrivFleet network boundary recon & runway projections

Hi team,

Kickoff for Acme.IO private fleet sizing — attaching an initial runway model and a rough network boundary map. High-level asks:

- We need a defendable sizing recommendation for a first-phase private pool (Prod) to meet these targets: 200 sustained req/s average per tenant, 2k req/s peak aggregated, 95th latency target <= 350ms tail for text-generation P95 on their typical 512-token prompt distribution.
- Call out headroom assumptions (burst factor, cache warmup, admission control thresholds).
- Identify networking constraints (egress bandwidth per node, cross-host KV sync limits) that would change node counts.
- Short list of operational mitigations we can promise in the SOW (pre-warmed lanes, staged canary scaling, explicit admission control thresholds).

Attachments: privfleet_runway_model.xlsx (baseline math), network_boundary_map.png, kv-cache-warmup.md

Ops@Acme is copied for visibility — they asked for a crisp capacity table and the likely hardware mix (they mentioned 8xA100-80GB racks as preferred).

Can you each add comments in the sheet and reply by EOD tomorrow with the recommended committed node counts, and an ops playbook snippet for surge handling?

Thanks,
Olga

On Tue, Dec 22, 2026 at 09:12 AM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kickoff for Acme.IO private fleet sizing — attaching an initial runway model and a rough network boundary map.

Thanks — I populated the workbook with a baseline lane model and three commitment scenarios (Conservative / Expected / Aggressive). Summary highlights:

- Baseline single node (8xA100-80GB) assumptions we used: steady-state serving throughput ≈ 60 req/s for a mixed 512-token workload when multiplexed across 4 lanes, with median per-request token cost ≈ 950 tokens. Peak per-node burst capacity (short term) ≈ 220 req/s before queueing latency blows past 95th target.
- To reach 200 sustained req/s for a single tenant without aggressive multiplexing we recommend reserving 4 nodes (Expected), with an Aggressive commit of 6 nodes for added headroom and easier warm-cache guarantees.
- Aggregated pool sizing for initial rollout (3 tenants concurrently active typical): Expected commit = 12 nodes, Aggressive = 18 nodes. Conservative = 8 nodes. See the sheet tab "CommitmentSummary" for the math and per-node assumptions.
- Network callouts: cross-host KV sync (for large-context sessions) adds ~200ms p95 when host-to-host RTT >2ms; where possible we should pin tenant lanes to hosts to avoid KV sync. If Acme demands free cross-host mobility, add 10-15% nodes as overhead for network-induced stalls.

I added a short ops snippet in the workbook with pre-warm steps: warm top-5 KV prefixes during deploy, prefill tokenizer caches, and an early admission-control threshold at 70% of measured per-node sustained throughput to trigger pre-scaling.

I'll also drop a compact runbook paragraph under the Drive link for ops@acme to consume.

- Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: PrivFleet network boundary recon & runway projections

Laura — good numbers. A few engineering caveats that will materially change node counts if Acme's topology is restrictive: 

1) Egress and cross-rack bandwidth: our tests show that model KV syncs and embedding batching over 25 Gbps links saturate earlier than compute. If their private racks only expose 10 Gbps per host, plan to add 1.3x nodes to avoid token-rate chop.

2) Burst headroom and admission control: recommend we set the pre-scale trigger at observed 60% sustained and 85% short-window (30s) to allow autoscaler to provision an extra 20% nodes before hitting queue depth thresholds. This maintains the 350ms P95 target under short surges.

3) Cache warmup and cold-start multiplier: quantify a cold-start penalty of 2.5x token-cost for the first 5 minutes after deploy for large-context prompts. Our ops mitigation: staged traffic migration + KV prefix prefill during deploy window.

4) Telemetry signals to trust: per-node qps, queue depth 99th, token throughput, and cross-host RTT percentile. We'll wire these into the canary gating rule set (INF-3421).

I added a quick simulation worksheet to the Drive folder that recomputes node counts under 10Gbps host link, 2.5x cold-start, and 1.2x peak multiplier. With those constraints the Expected commit becomes 16 nodes (vs 12).

- Vivek (Infra)

Appreciate the rapid turn. Quick synthesis and next steps for Acme.IO:

1) Recommended initial commit (we'll present these as three options in the SOW):
   - Conservative: 8 nodes (parked lanes + minimal warmup)
   - Expected: 12 nodes (pinning lanes to hosts, proactive prefill, 70% pre-scale trigger)
   - Aggressive / Gold: 18 nodes (dedicated warm pool, 15% buffer, SLA support)

2) Network boundary notes for the SOW: if host link <= 10Gbps, add 1.3x nodes to account for KV and egress constraints; if Acme requires cross-host mobility, add 10-15% overhead.

3) Ops commitments to include in the SOW: staged canary scaling plan (step adds: +20% nodes with 5 minute warm window), KV prefix prefill during deploys, admission control thresholds (60% sustained / 85% short-window), telemetry gating (qps/queue depth/rtp).

4) Action items:
   - Laura: finalize the CommitmentSummary tab with the conservative/expected/aggressive numbers and cost mapping to SKUs (due 2026-12-28).
   - Vivek: add the 10Gbps simulation sheet and the autoscaler trigger spec to INF-3421 (due 2026-12-27).
   - Markus: prepare the procurement one-pager and Gold SLA paragraph (due 2026-12-29).

I'll set a 30-minute review with Acme ops for Tue 2026-12-29 10:00 PT. ops@acme.io — can you confirm availability?

Thanks everyone — this should get us to a clean SOW baseline and avoid last-minute add-ons.

Olga
